unit_id: 1_在PD结构中引入二氧化硫对通孔镀铜的影响#0003
text: In this study, SO was used to chemically modify the commonly used leveling agent polydimethyldiallylammonium (PD) in through-hole electroplating, resulting in a more effective leveling agent, PDS, which improved the throwing power (TP), leading to through-hole circuit boards with better metal coverage in difficult-to-reach areas. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental studies were conducted to understand how the −SO structure influences the leveling ability of the leveling agent.

unit_id: 1_在PD结构中引入二氧化硫对通孔镀铜的影响#0004
text: Furthermore, theoretical and experimental studies were conducted to understand how the −SO structure influences the leveling ability of the leveling agent. The study demonstrates that the −SO - modified additive significantly enhances the copper plating process, resulting in thicker and more uniform deposits in through-holes, which are critical for ensuring high-quality circuit boards.Additionally, this study elu cidates the mechanism of action of the leveling agent on the copper surface, providing theoretical support for the development of copper plating leveling agents.

The leveling ability differences between the leveling agents PD and PDS were investigated using Cyclic Voltammetry, constant current method, and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy.

unit_id: 1_在PD结构中引入二氧化硫对通孔镀铜的影响#0006
text: The leveling ability differences between the leveling agents PD and PDS were investigated using Cyclic Voltammetry, constant current method, and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy. Additionally, the optimal concentrations of the additives were determined. Quantum chemical calculations were employed to analyze the electrostatic potential, HOMO/LUMO orbitals, and differential charge density on the Cu (111) surface for both leveling agents. These theoretical analyses provided insights into the reasons behind the differing leveling abilities of the two agents.

text: Currently, the most widely used technology in the through-hole plating process of circuit boards is acid copper plating, which typically involves a conventional acid copper plating solution containing copper sulfate, sulfuric acid, and trace amounts of plating additives[10]. Traditional electroplating additives can be categorized into suppressors, accelerators, and levelers[11–13].

unit_id: 1_在PD结构中引入二氧化硫对通孔镀铜的影响#0012
text: Traditional electroplating additives can be categorized into suppressors, accelerators, and levelers[11–13]. In the context of through-hole electroplating, the key substance capable of enhancing the TP value is the leveler, which, as a crucial component in the acid copper plating solution, requires only a small addition to effectively increase the TP value [14,15]. As a critical metric for assessing the performance of throughhole copper plating, the TP value is calculated as the ratio of the copper thickness on the surface to the copper layer thickness inside the hole [16].

Electrochemical experiments were conducted to compare the leveling capabilities of the two additive molecules, and their optimal working concentrations were determined.

text: This study improves the common leveling agent PD used in acid copper plating by incorporating SO_2 and investigates the leveling performance of both leveling agents through CVS, GMs, EIS testing, and more. The introduction of the −-S0_2 structure effectively enhances the leveling capability of the leveling agent and creates new active sites on the Cu surface. The enhancement of leveling capabilities by the intro duction of the -s0_2 structure was further substantiated through differential charge density calculations.

Additionally, electrochemical experiments confirmed that the optimal concentration for both PD and PDS is 100 mg/L. SEM observations of the copper layers plated at this concentration revealed a significant reduction in porosity, indicating that both additive molecules effectively decrease the porosity of the plating layer.

unit_id: 1_在PD结构中引入二氧化硫对通孔镀铜的影响#0097
text: This study demonstrates that the introduction of the −-SO_2 functional group into PD leveling agents significantly improves their leveling performance. Theoretical calculations reveal that the -SO_2 group enhances molecular adsorption and introduces additional interaction sites, leading to a more uniform adsorption layer and stronger inhibition of Cu ^2 + deposition.Furthermore, comparative experiments show that the SO_2^- modified PD exhibits superior leveling efficiency and deposit uniformity compared to commercially available leveling agents.
